Leads only (403 not_permitted otherwise). Approve each item's generated version, one item at a time, with the
single fast-track's checks, at the version in `seen_versions`; every item needs an entry (else 422). Anything
that can't be fast-tracked (open findings, not in needs_rereview, a newer version than the one seen) is listed in
`skipped` with its error code and stays in the normal lane (ruling 4).

with `details.reason`.

post.description: Manual assignment by a lead, or a reviewer handing off their own item. Null returns it to the pool.

A reviewer takes an item (from the pool, or their own) and starts reviewing it: submitted or
needs_rereview -> in_review. Leads may claim anyone's.

Approve, approve with edits, request changes, or reject the current version. Every decision needs a
reason. Approvals also need every finding triaged (409 open_findings_block_decision; plain Approve also
409 accepted_findings_block_approval), the AI check finished (409 ai_check_pending; failed needs
llm_override_reason), and current offer terms (409 stale_offer_terms). Approve with edits may answer 409
findings_need_triage with v+1's new findings (v+1 is kept). A newer version is 409 stale_version.

post.description: Build the evidence pack zip (files, hashes, history) in the background; poll `getExport`.

One-click approval of a needs_rereview item's generated terms-change version (`version_n`, the version the
reviewer saw; else 409 stale_version). The item's assignee or a lead. The usual gates apply: 409
open_findings_block_decision, accepted_findings_block_approval, stale_offer_terms; 409 conflict if the current
version isn't a generated one; 409 invalid_transition unless the item is in needs_rereview.

get.description: Findings on the current version, or on `version_n`.

post.description:
Run a failed AI check again on the current version (reviewer or lead, while the item is under review).
It starts as `pending`; poll the item for the result.
withdrawn or expired -> submitted with v+1 (a copy of the current version unless text is given).
The submitter (or a lead) records where the approved version runs. Approved items only.
Request takedown of live content; the item goes to withdrawn (ruling 6).

needs_rereview -> approved on the same version with a fresh expiry. The code checks re-run first; new
findings come back as 409 findings_need_triage. A drift_detected re-review is 409 drift_not_restored until the
placement's latest check finds the approved copy again.
Submit v+1 after changes were requested: bumps the round, back to the previous reviewer. Submitter only.
